29: Astrid and Tomás walk to school and the street is full of noise: a red bus, three cars, one bike and a very big lorry. Stop! says Astrid at the corner. Look left, look right, listen. The light is red — wait. Now the light is green — cross! Tomás wants to run, but in the street we walk. What can you see in YOUR street? Learn the rules and cross safely with them!
30: Beach day! Nico builds a giant castle with wet sand and puts one shell on every tower. The sun is hot, so he wears his blue hat and eats a very fast ice cream before it melts. And Pip? Pip swims like a champion, up and down, up and down — he is a sea bird after all. Do you like the beach? What do you do there? Take your hat and come to the sand!
31: Weather window game! Every morning Freya looks outside and says the weather. Today it is windy: the trees are dancing and her hat flies away. Yesterday it was rainy and she needed her red umbrella. When it is sunny they go out, when it is cold they stay in with hot chocolate. Look — after the rain, a rainbow! Is it sunny or rainy where YOU are? Look out and tell us!
32: Seven days, seven plans! On Monday Astrid has swimming. On Wednesday Nico has music, and he sings very loudly. On Friday they have art, the best day of the week. And on Saturday? Pancakes and no homework! Sunday is for the family. Which day do you like best? Say your favourite day and tell us what you do on it!
33: The sun says good morning and the moon says good night. In the morning Tomás wakes up, eats his breakfast and runs to school. In the afternoon he plays outside. In the evening he reads a book, and at night he sleeps — well, almost. Pip sleeps all day and wakes up at night, because puffins have their own clock! What do you do in the morning? Tell us your day!
34: Good morning! Freya has milk and bread with jam for breakfast, and one banana to take to school. Astrid has an egg and a glass of juice. The spoon falls, the milk goes on the table, and everybody laughs. Breakfast makes the day happy — and long, if you eat slowly like Freya. What do YOU have for breakfast? Sit down with them and say it in English!
35: Lunchbox surprise! What is inside today? There is a sandwich with cheese, there is one red apple and there are two biscuits. There is a small bottle of water and a paper napkin. But in Nico's box there are only carrots — his mother wins today! Tomás shares his biscuits, because friends share. What is in YOUR lunchbox? Open it and tell us!
36: Happy birthday to Astrid! There are eight candles on the cake, one for every year. How old are you? Eight! She closes her eyes, makes a secret wish and blows — and all the candles go out at once. There are balloons everywhere, there are presents on the table, and everybody sings. Pip eats a piece of cake bigger than his head. How old are YOU? Come to the party!
37: The moving song! Shake your hands, nod your head, raise your arms, wave to your friend. Stamp your feet — louder! Wiggle your fingers, touch your ears, close your eyes… and open them again. Tomás does everything twice as fast and Freya does everything twice as slowly, so the song never ends the same way. Stand up: can you do all the actions with them?
38: Animal talents! Birds can fly high over the sea. Fish can swim, and they never get tired. Monkeys can climb the tallest trees, dogs can run very fast, and cats can sleep for hours and hours. Nico wants to know: can a puffin sing? Pip opens his beak… and everybody covers their ears! What can animals do? Come and find out with Nico and Pip!
39: Big numbers now! Astrid and Tomás count the stairs of the lighthouse: eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen… Tomás is already tired at fifteen. Sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen — and twenty at the top, with the whole sea in front of them. How many stairs are there in your school? Count with them, from eleven to twenty!
40: A-B-C-D… the alphabet song! Freya knows all twenty-six letters and she sings them very fast. A is the first letter, Z is the last one. Big letters for names, small letters for the rest. Pip stops on the letter P, because P is for Pip, P is for puffin — his two favourite words. Can you sing the whole alphabet? Take a big breath and start with Freya!
41: N-I-C-O! Spelling your name is like a little song. How do you spell your name? asks Astrid, with her pencil ready. Nico spells it fast, too fast, and Astrid writes NIKO. Again, please — slowly! Letter by letter, they write every name in the class, and every surname too. How do YOU spell your name? Listen, say it slowly and write it down!
42: Grammar magic with Astrid and Freya! HE is for a boy: he is my brother, he is a doctor. SHE is for a girl: she is my friend, she is a teacher. And IT? IT is for things and animals: it is a fish, it is a book. He is, she is, it is — three little words that say who everybody is. Who is in your class? Point at them and say it correctly!
43: THIS ball is here, in Tomás's hand. THAT bird is there, far away in the sky. These shoes are near, those clouds are far. Nico gets everything wrong on purpose: this house! — while pointing at a mountain. Everybody laughs and corrects him, and that is how you learn. Near or far? Here or there? Point at something and say it with them!
44: The magic word game! Two teams, a pile of word cards and one golden star for the winner. Freya's team points at the pictures and guesses fast; Nico's team guesses even faster, but they shout the words in the wrong order. Point, guess, clap! Pip is the referee, and Pip is not very fair. Do you remember all the words of the course? Choose a team and play!
45: Forty-five units — the Lighthouse Explorers did it! There is a party at the lighthouse tonight: balloons on the stairs, music, and a certificate with a golden star for every explorer. Freya, Nico, Astrid and Tomás sing and dance, and Pip stands on the top of the lighthouse like a tiny lamp. They are proud, and they are friends. And YOU did it too. Come and celebrate!
